svg.title: Neptune Pass sediment budget: the Quarantine Bay deposit exceeded sediment scoured from the pass
svg.desc: Estimated sediment volumes from Kolker and colleagues (2025): 6.1 million cubic meters scoured from Neptune Pass, 11 million cubic meters deposited in Quarantine Bay, or roughly 4.8 million cubic meters of net deposition. Estimates use different survey years and model assumptions. This is not a measurement of permanent dry land.
svg.text: The sediment that came from elsewhere
Neptune Pass and Quarantine Bay · Estimated sediment volumes
≈4.8 million m³ additional net deposition, after rounding
2016–2022 channel surveys vs. 2011–2022 bay surveys; volumes are estimates, not a direct sediment inventory.
Assumptions include survey interpolation, 22 mm/year subsidence, and sediment-porosity sensitivity.
Source: Kolker et al., PLOS ONE 20(4), e0320502 (2025), §3.7, Table 3 · doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0320502
Original diagram © Final Vestige Studios · Not a measure of permanent land or of 2026 conditions
